title: Slippage parameter does not protect claimer against adverse discount-rate / exchange-rate changes (claimer overpays)
justification: Value leak with stated assumptions per C4 Medium. The slippage parameter minRewardTokenSupplied is one-sided (lower bound on amount paid) but the bot/claimer's economic risk is OVERPAYING. Owner mid-flight changes (discount-rate decrease, exchange-rate increase) OR MEV sandwiching of those owner state changes leave the claimer paying more than simulated. Demoted from author High estimate because exploitation requires either owner action (centralized vector covered separately) or MEV sandwich of owner state changes — claimer can defend by tighter quoting if interface exposes both bounds.
preconditions: Owner mutates discount/exchange/pause state between simulation and inclusion, OR MEV searcher front-runs claim with owner state change.
impact: Claimer pays full price for zero or negative profit; in-flight bots are forced into unprofitable trades.
attack_path_summary: 1) Bot quotes 14.7 USDC for 15 USD yield at 2% discount, sets minRewardTokenSupplied=14.7. 2) Owner sets discount=0 (or raises exchangeRate). 3) actualPayment becomes 15.0; check actualPayment >= 14.7 passes. 4) Claimer pays full price for zero margin.
